name: Reconcile Cluster
description: Top-level Reconcile loop: validates the spec, provisions TLS/RBAC/Services/ConfigMap, applies the server StatefulSet (holding replicas during a scale-down drain), collects diagnostics once the cluster has formed, and marks the cluster Ready once formation and rollout are both verified — or hands a cluster that is short of servers to the shortfall assessment.

name: Reconcile Standalone
description: Top-level standalone reconcile: validates the spec (including admin-secret password shape), reconciles TLS/ConfigMap/Service/StatefulSet/Ingress, runs a pre-upgrade health check on image-tag drift, and updates status once the StatefulSet reports one ready replica.

name: Merge Env Vars
description: Computes the StatefulSet container's next env-var list: applies the cluster controller's desired vars, drops names in the previously-owned annotation that are no longer desired, and preserves foreign vars added by plugin/fleet/Aura controllers.

name: Collect Cluster Diagnostics
description: Runs SHOW SERVERS and SHOW DATABASES against a cluster that has formed — Ready, Degraded, or mid-rollout with ClusterFormed=True, so it keeps reporting while a server is down —, fills the address of a server that is down from the per-cluster address book (SHOW SERVERS reports none for it), and writes results plus ServersHealthy/DatabasesHealthy conditions into status.diagnostics; non-fatal — every error is surfaced only in status.diagnostics.collectionError, never returned to the caller.

name: Collect Standalone Diagnostics
description: Runs SHOW DATABASES (plus users/roles) against a Ready standalone instance and writes status.diagnostics; non-fatal, mirroring the cluster path's collectionError-only error handling.

name: Collect Users And Roles
description: Runs SHOW USERS and SHOW ROLES, sorts and caps each result list at 50 rows, and appends any query failure to the shared collectionError string without aborting the rest of diagnostics collection (e.g. when the connecting user lacks SHOW USER/SHOW ROLE privilege).

name: Advance Rolling Upgrade
description: Dispatches exactly one non-blocking state-machine step per reconcile (Staging, Rolling, Stabilizing, Verifying) and re-stages from any active phase if the target image tag changes mid-flight, so an in-flight upgrade never blocks reconciliation of other clusters. Each phase transition restarts status.upgradeStatus.phaseStartTime and records the ended phase's duration in neo4j_operator_upgrade_duration_seconds exactly once, derived from the persisted phaseStartTime.

name: Pause Or Fail Rolling Upgrade
description: Routes a failed upgrade step to a terminal Paused state (manual intervention required, never auto-resumed) when upgradeStrategy.autoPauseOnFailure is set, or to Failed so image drift can retry the upgrade automatically once the underlying problem is resolved. The phase that was active when the step failed is recorded in neo4j_operator_upgrade_duration_seconds.

name: Verify Version Upgrade
description: Confirms every Enabled server in SHOW SERVERS reports the target image version, applying a kernel-alias normalization for the one CalVer release (2025.01.x) that self-reports as kernel 5.27.x, before the upgrade is allowed to complete.

name: Detect Split Brain
description: Queries each running server pod's own SHOW SERVERS view, groups pods that see similar cluster configurations, and flags a split-brain when a minority group's servers are not a subset of the majority group's visible servers. Runs only on a cluster that has been healthy: phase Ready or Degraded.

name: Restart Orphaned Pods
description: Repairs a detected split-brain by deleting the orphaned pods (or, in the nuclear-option repair action, every server pod) so the StatefulSet recreates them and they rejoin the majority cluster view.

name: Drain Server For Scale-Down
description: Drives one cordon/deallocate/wait/drop step per reconcile for servers being removed by a topology scale-down, gating on a DEALLOCATE dry-run and the system database's minimum-voting-member floor before ever cordoning a server.

name: Plan Scale-Down Step
description: Pure decision function that inspects the live State/Hosting of each drain-target server and picks the single next drain action (cordon, deallocate, wait, or drop) for the caller to execute — a draining server hosting only `system` is droppable even if stuck in Deallocating.

name: Expand Cluster Storage
description: Compares each server-StatefulSet PVC's current size against spec.storage.size, rejects any shrink attempt, and on growth patches the PVCs then orphan-deletes the StatefulSet so it is recreated with the updated VolumeClaimTemplates.

name: Expand Standalone Storage
description: Standalone twin of sf-expand-storage: compares the neo4j-data PVC size against spec.storage.size, rejects shrinks, and patches plus orphan-deletes the single-replica StatefulSet on growth so it is recreated with the enlarged claim template.

name: Check Storage Expansion Needed
description: Compares desired PVC storage size from spec.storage.size against the live PVCs' storage requests and reports match, expand, or shrink so the caller can decide whether to proceed, no-op, or hard-reject.

name: Calculate Topology Placement
description: Determines whether topology-spread and/or anti-affinity should be applied, auto-discovers availability zones from cluster-scoped Nodes when none are configured, and degrades to best-effort zone spread (rather than failing) when node listing is unavailable in namespace-scoped installs.

name: Apply Topology Constraints
description: Applies the calculated topology-spread constraints and/or pod anti-affinity rules onto the server StatefulSet's pod template before it is created or updated.

name: Verify Cluster Formation
description: Checks Bolt connectivity (tracking a consecutive-failure streak for outage forensics), then runs split-brain detection with a legacy SHOW SERVERS count fallback to decide whether the cluster has formed with the expected number of Enabled+Available servers. Returns the SHOW SERVERS list it saw and whether the shortfall is a split-brain, for the shortfall assessment.

name: Hold Image Drift Until Ready
description: While the cluster is not Ready, pins the in-memory spec image back to whatever the live StatefulSet currently runs so the normal reconcile path can't apply a version change outside the upgrade state machine, unless zero replicas are ready (nothing to protect).

name: Is Upgrade Required
description: Detects image drift on the server StatefulSet (or a stalled Failed-phase retry whose target and status.version still disagree) to decide whether a new rolling upgrade should start; never fires while Paused, already mid-flight, or while a server is unavailable (Degraded condition True), since rolling the others could cost the cluster its majority.

name: Ensure Seed Credentials Projected
description: Validates that a hosting cluster or standalone CR's spec.extraEnvFrom projects the cloud-credentials Secret a seedURI restore needs, auto-patching it in (and triggering a rolling restart) only when the CR carries the neo4j.com/auto-inherit-seed-creds annotation.

name: Ensure PVC Seed Proxy
description: Idempotently creates the busybox-httpd Deployment, Service, and NetworkPolicy that expose a backup PVC over HTTP so Neo4j's URLConnectionSeedProvider can seed a database from it during a restore; the policy admits only the target's server pods (a cluster's neo4j.com/cluster label, a standalone's app label). The provider fetches one file, so a differential's chain is merged first (sf-merge-seed-chain).

name: Merge PVC Backup Chain for Seeding
description: newSeedMergePlan / applySeedMerge (pvc_seed_merge.go): when a PVC seed artifact is not recorded as a FULL backup, the seed proxy pod gets a merge-chain init container running the target's Neo4j image that copies the chain to scratch space (emptyDir or spec.options.tempStorage), merges it with neo4j-admin database aggregate-backup (5.x) / backup aggregate (CalVer), and publishes the merged full artifact at the original relative path; a failed merge fails the restore at once with neo4j-admin's reason (rule 109).

name: Reconcile Neo4jDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec inline, resolves the target host, checks readiness, projects seed credentials if needed, and ensures the database exists.

name: Create Or Verify Database
description: ensureDatabase() checks DatabaseExists, then issues CREATE DATABASE (plain, with TOPOLOGY, or from seedURI/seedURIs via OPTIONS) and refreshes status.state/status.servers from SHOW DATABASES. resolveDatabaseCreateInputs() decides the host-dependent inputs once for every create path: spec.defaultCypherLanguage is sent as DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER only when the target image is CalVer (neo4j.DefaultLanguageForImage; the 5.26 LTS has no such clause, so it is omitted), and spec.topology is ignored for a standalone host. All four create methods render through one statement builder.

name: Alter Database Topology
description: internal/neo4j/client.go's AlterDatabaseTopology issues ALTER DATABASE `name` SET TOPOLOGY n PRIMARIES m SECONDARIES for a post-bootstrap topology change; a capability of the Neo4j client, not currently auto-invoked from the Neo4jDatabase reconcile loop (CLAUDE.md documents it as an operator-triggered change).

name: Drop Database On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() resolves the host and issues DROP DATABASE for spec.name, releasing the finalizer on success or on a non-retryable failure. After a successful drop it lists Neo4jRoles on the same clusterRef and warns (non-fatally) on each role whose spec still grants on the dropped database, case-insensitively.

name: Import Initial Data
description: importInitialData() executes each spec.initialData.cypherStatements entry against the new database once, skipped when the database was created from a seedURI.

name: Update Neo4jDatabase Status
description: updateDatabaseStatus() re-fetches the CR under retry.RetryOnConflict and sets the Ready condition, status.phase, and status.message.

name: Reconcile Neo4jDatabaseAlias
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec inline, resolves clusterRef, waits for the target database to exist, then compares the live alias (if any) against spec.targetDatabase.

name: Create Alias
description: Issues CREATE ALIAS when ShowAlias reports no existing alias with this name, pinned to Cypher 5 so the server's default language cannot change how a dotted name is read.

name: Retarget Alias
description: Issues ALTER ALIAS ... SET TARGET when the live alias's database differs from spec.targetDatabase (drift correction; spec wins).

name: Drop Alias On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() issues DROP ALIAS IF EXISTS unless spec.deletionPolicy=Retain; a failed drop releases the finalizer rather than wedging deletion.

name: Reconcile Neo4jShardedDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves the referenced cluster, checks property-sharding readiness, opens a Neo4j client, and drives seed resolution plus create/status refresh.

name: Create Sharded Database
description: createShardedDatabase() executes the statement buildCreateShardedDatabaseCypher() renders: `CYPHER 25 CREATE DATABASE ... SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 25 SET GRAPH SHARD {...} SET PROPERTY SHARDS {...} OPTIONS {...}`, binding every seed/user-supplied value as a driver parameter. The language clause is always emitted: shard sub-databases inherit the parent's language, and the server no longer forces CYPHER_25 for sharding.

name: Drop Sharded Database For Replace
description: dropShardedDatabaseIfExists() issues `CYPHER 25 DROP DATABASE ... IF EXISTS DESTROY DATA WAIT`, gated to the spec.replaceExisting+force path and guarded by status.lastDestructiveRestoreGeneration so it never re-fires at the same generation.

name: Stamp Server Default Cypher Language
description: stampClusterCypherLanguage()/stampStandaloneCypherLanguage() resolve spec.serverDefaultCypherLanguage (resources.StampServerCypherLanguage) from the spec, a legacy db.query.default_language key, the existing stamp, the image line, whether the StatefulSet exists and the value in the current ConfigMap, and persist it to status.effectiveCypherLanguage before the ConfigMap that renders it is built (internal/controller/server_cypher_language.go).

name: Resolve And Serve Sharded Seed
description: resolveShardedSeed()/resolvePVCShardedSeed() turn spec.seedBackupRef into either per-shard cloud seedURIs or an operator-managed PVC seed-proxy Deployment+Service serving each shard's .backup file over HTTP. A PVC run with a shard recorded as DIFF is refused before the proxy starts (Neo4j seeds a sharded database over HTTP only from full backups, and merging drops the sharding header); the requeue seeds once a full run lands. For a cloud seed, ensureClusterSeedConfig() projects the backup's credentials and custom endpoint onto the cluster under the auto-inherit annotation and waits for the rollout.

name: Update Shard Status
description: updateShardStatus() reads SHOW DATABASES once per reconcile and records, from those rows only, status.graphShard (`{name}-g000`), status.propertyShards (`{name}-pNNN`, ordered by index), status.virtualDatabase (the logical database) and status.creationTime (set once when the graph shard is first seen; restarted by a destructive recreate). Per-shard state is online only when every copy is online; ready means at least one copy is online and none that should be online is not. The write is skipped when nothing changed and failures are non-fatal. Shard size, servers, lastError, propertyCount, the virtual database's endpoint and metrics, and status.totalSize stay unpopulated because SHOW DATABASES does not carry them.

name: Reconcile Neo4jReplicaDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves clusterRef, checks the version gate for cross-cluster replicas, then OBSERVES the live database's type before dispatching on source.mode to create (backup or network), reporting, or terminally marking it promoted. While the database is still a replica it publishes the lag SHOW DATABASES reports (a transaction count) as neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions{namespace,cluster_name,replica,database,k8s_cluster}, and removes that series whenever it cannot vouch for it: when the CR is deleted, found gone, or promoted, when the database has vanished from the server, and when the downstream cluster is missing, not Ready or too old for replicas, the Neo4j client cannot connect, the database lookup fails, or the spec fails validation. The next successful observation sets the gauge again. The Neo4j client is obtained through an injectable factory (replicaNeo4jClient) so these branches are testable without a Bolt server.

name: Create Replica Database From Backup
description: Calls CreateReplicaDatabaseFromBackup with the upstream database, pull/seed URI, and optional topology when the target database does not yet exist (source.mode: backup). pullURI is either set directly or resolved by sf-resolve-upstream-backup-ref from source.upstreamBackupRef.

name: Detect Out-Of-Band Promotion
description: markPromoted() records the terminal Promoted phase the moment the live database's `type` column is observed to no longer be replica, whether caused by this operator's own Neo4jReplicaPromotion or an external actor. Removes the replica's neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions series, since a promoted database no longer replicates.

name: Drop Replica Database On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() re-checks the live database type and only issues DROP DATABASE while it is still type=replica; a promoted database is retained instead. Removes the replica's neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions series whatever the outcome.

name: Promote Replica Database
description: Reconcile() runs CHECK (live type=replica) -> PROMOTE (PromoteReplicaDatabase) -> CHECK (type no longer replica) -> RECORD, so a crash between the call and the status write is recovered as an idempotent success rather than a repeat promote. The terminal Completed/Failed phase latches: the first write that persists it increments neo4j_operator_replica_promotions_total{namespace,cluster_name,result,k8s_cluster} exactly once (result=success or failure) and later or stale reconciles count nothing; a successful promotion also removes the replica's lag series.

name: Reconcile Neo4jBackup
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec (including replication-source chain rules), resolves the target cluster/standalone, checks readiness/suspend, runs sharded preflight, and branches to the scheduled or one-time backup path.

name: Create One-Time Backup Job
description: createBackupJob() creates exactly one Kubernetes Job per Neo4jBackup CR running `neo4j-admin database backup` (invariant: Job-per-CR, never a long-running backup pod/StatefulSet). With options.splitArchivePartSize on a 2026.09+ target it adds --split-archive-part-size=<bytes>; on an older target the Job is refused with a message naming the field.

name: Create Scheduled Backup CronJob
description: createBackupCronJob() creates/updates one CronJob per Neo4jBackup CR with spec.schedule set; each firing spawns its own child Job (still Job-per-run, never a persistent backup pod).

name: Record Backup Run Outcome
description: recordOneShotBackupRun() / reconcileScheduledHistory() observe a completed Job's conditions, parse its pod log, and append a BackupRun to status.history, deferring finalization until restore-critical artifact filenames are captured, including each artifact's FULL/DIFF type (status.history[].artifactType, databaseArtifacts[].type, shardArtifacts[].type), warning when a sharded run on a PVC wrote a differential shard.

name: Parse Backup Pod Log
description: neo4jbackup_log_parser.go's regex-based parsers extract per-shard/per-database .backup filenames, sizes, whether each artifact is FULL or DIFF (from neo4j-admin's 'full/differential backup of database' lines; an AUTO run that fell back to a full is FULL), and neo4j-admin backup validate results from a completed backup pod's stdout.

name: Cleanup Backup Artifacts
description: cleanupBackupArtifacts() runs an alpine-based cleanup Job (deterministic UID-derived name) enforcing spec.retention (maxCount/maxAge) against a PVC-backed chain directory; cloud storage retention is delegated to bucket lifecycle rules. Counts *.backup artifacts but deletes each one together with its split-archive parts (x.backup.*).

name: Reconcile Neo4jRestore
description: Main reconcile loop: resolves the target, checks terminal phases and version compatibility, and either polls in-flight progress or starts a fresh restore attempt.

name: Start Restore
description: startRestore() validates the request, pins the resolved backup source onto status, and routes it: online (Cypher recreate/create with a seedURI, or the all-databases loop) for every cluster and for most standalone restores; the offline neo4j-admin Job (stopping the instance first when spec.stopCluster is set) only for a standalone restore that cannot be seeded online — point-in-time, a source.type storage path, cloud storage by pod identity, or a Job restore already holding the instance (rule 108). The offline path emits an event naming the reason.

name: Route Restore Online or Offline
description: standaloneOfflineReason() / restoreRunsOffline() / restoreOnJobPath() (restore_target.go) decide, from the pinned status.resolvedSource, whether a restore runs online or takes the offline neo4j-admin Job: a cluster never takes the Job; a standalone does only for point-in-time, source.type storage, an unrecorded artifact, cloud storage with no credentialsSecretRef, or a Job restore that already holds its neo4j.com/restore-in-progress marker. The reason is reported in the refusal and the RestoreStarted event (rule 108).

name: Create Offline Standalone Restore Job
description: createRestoreJob() builds and creates the offline `neo4j-admin database restore` Job used only for a Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone restore that cannot run online (rule 108: point-in-time, a source.type storage path, cloud storage by pod identity) (neo4j-admin restore --overwrite-destination is documented as unsafe on clusters). --from-path names the exact artifact whenever it is known (backupPath ending in .backup, or the pinned snapshot's recorded file or per-database entry for the source database) — the only form neo4j-admin restores under a different name; otherwise it globs the source database's newest file (PVC) or passes the cloud directory (same name only).

name: Online Cypher Restore
description: startClusterCypherRestore() restores one database online against the running DBMS — on a cluster and on a standalone (rule 108): dbms.[cluster.]recreateDatabase with a seedURI over an existing database, CREATE DATABASE … OPTIONS {seedURI} for a new one, then polls SHOW DATABASE until every allocation is online. Target-specific plumbing (StatefulSet name, pod labels for the seed proxy's NetworkPolicy, the CR that carries seed spec.env/extraEnvFrom) comes from restoreTarget. A PVC differential is merged by the seed proxy first (the proxy serves one file over HTTP; Neo4j refuses a DIFF without its chain); it runs pre-restore hooks before issuing and post-restore hooks once online; never a Job on cluster targets.

name: All-Databases Restore Loop
description: startAllDatabasesRestore() drives one per-database CREATE/recreate-with-seedURI action per reconcile pass from the resolved backup's per-database artifact map, on clusters and standalones, tracking progress in status.databaseResults; runs pre-restore hooks once per attempt (neo4j.com/restore-pre-hooks-ran) and post-restore hooks before Completed, has the seed proxy merge each database's PVC chain that is not recorded as FULL, and stamps status.completionTime. Property-sharded families are excluded and must restore via their own Neo4jShardedDatabase CR.

name: Handle Restore Success
description: handleRestoreSuccess() restarts a stopped cluster, registers/starts the restored database(s) (or all restored databases), runs post-restore hooks, and forces a cross-server recreate-from-seed so every server converges on the restored server-0 data.

name: Resolve Cluster Reference
description: ResolveClusterRef() looks up a clusterRef, trying Neo4jEnterpriseCluster first and falling back to Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone of the same name, returning a ResolvedTarget with IsReady()/NewClient() helpers. IsReady() accepts a cluster whose phase is Ready or Degraded, or whose Ready condition is True (clusterAcceptsWork), so dependents keep working against a cluster that is serving with a majority of its servers.

name: Resolve Backup Reference
description: ResolveBackupRef() dereferences a Neo4jBackup CR name into a concrete StorageLocation and the BackupsPath of its most recent Succeeded run, returning a wrapped ErrBackupNotReady when no Succeeded run exists yet.

name: Reconcile Neo4jUser
description: Drives a Neo4jUser to its desired state each loop: validates the spec (routing a not-yet-applied password Secret to Pending, not Failed), resolves the clusterRef target, creates or ALTERs the Neo4j user over Bolt, diffs granted vs. desired roles and issues GRANT/REVOKE ROLE, then records RolesSynced/PasswordSynced conditions and the Ready phase.

name: Reconcile Neo4jRole
description: Drives a Neo4jRole to its desired state each loop: validates the spec, creates the role if absent (refusing built-ins without adoptBuiltin), normalises spec.privileges to Neo4j's stored rendering (sf-normalise-role-privileges) and diffs that against live SHOW ROLE PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS output, applies missing GRANT/DENY statements verbatim, and derives REVOKE statements textually for privileges no longer desired (never revoking immutable ones). Before applying, it resolves each missing grant's database names against SHOW DATABASES and aliases (case-insensitively) and skips grants naming a database that does not exist, reporting them via PrivilegesResolve=False instead of failing the reconcile; they apply once the database exists.

name: Render Privilege Rules
description: rolePrivilegeStatements() renders each spec.privilegeRules entry with neo4j.RenderPrivilegeRule (backtick-escaped names, one segment) and appends it to spec.privileges, so every downstream path — normalisation, learn mode, resolve reporting, the dropped-database warning — sees one desired set. A Neo4jDatabase watch re-queues roles naming that database (internal/controller/neo4jrole_rules.go).

name: Reconcile Neo4jRoleBinding
description: Drives a Neo4jRoleBinding to its desired state each loop: verifies the target Neo4j user already exists (bindings never create/drop users), resolves Neo4jRole CR names to Neo4j role names, and diffs/grants/revokes role membership — non-exclusive by default, but always revoking roles this binding previously granted that were removed from spec.roles.

name: Reconcile Neo4jAuthRule
description: Drives a Neo4jAuthRule to its desired state each loop: gates on the cluster running Neo4j 2026.03+ and configuring an OIDC authorization provider, then CREATE OR REPLACEs the rule's condition/enabled flag (which clears prior grants) and re-grants the desired role set via GRANT/REVOKE ROLES ... TO/FROM AUTH RULE.

name: Create Neo4j user
description: CreateUserAdvanced issues CREATE USER `name` IF NOT EXISTS with staged SET PASSWORD/SET STATUS/SET HOME DATABASE/SET AUTH clauses against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Alter Neo4j user
description: AlterUser issues ALTER USER with REMOVE clauses ordered before SET clauses (password, password-change-required, suspended status, home database, external auth providers) against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Drop Neo4j user
description: DropUserIfExists issues DROP USER `name` IF EXISTS against the system database, making user removal idempotent (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Grant role to user
description: GrantRoleToUser issues GRANT ROLE `role` TO `user` against the system database (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Revoke role from user
description: RevokeRoleFromUser issues REVOKE ROLE `role` FROM `user` against the system database (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Create Neo4j role
description: CreateRoleAdvanced issues CREATE ROLE `name` [IF NOT EXISTS] [AS COPY OF `copyOf`] against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Drop Neo4j role
description: DropRoleIfExists issues DROP ROLE `name` IF EXISTS against the system database; built-in roles are never dropped by any caller (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Apply privilege statement
description: ExecutePrivilegeStatement runs the role's original (non-canonicalised) GRANT/DENY privilege statement text as auto-commit Cypher against the system database, with bounded retry on transient GQLSTATUS 25N11 conflicting-transaction errors (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Revoke privilege statement
description: Runs a REVOKE statement derived textually from the role's currently-applied GRANT/DENY command via DerivePrivilegeRevoke (internal/neo4j/privileges.go) through ExecutePrivilegeStatement — REVOKEs are never accepted directly from Neo4jRole.spec.privileges, and immutable privileges are skipped rather than attempted.

name: Show role privileges
description: ShowRolePrivileges runs SHOW ROLE `name` PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS YIELD command, immutable (falling back to a legacy projection without immutable on older Neo4j) to read a role's currently-applied privilege set from the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Create or replace auth rule
description: CreateOrReplaceAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 CREATE OR REPLACE AUTH RULE `name` SET CONDITION <expr> SET ENABLED true|false against the system database, subsuming ALTER semantics by replacing the rule outright (and clearing its prior role grants) (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Grant roles to auth rule
description: GrantRolesToAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 GRANT ROLES r1, r2, ... TO AUTH RULE `name` against the system database (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Revoke roles from auth rule
description: RevokeRolesFromAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 REVOKE ROLES r1, r2, ... FROM AUTH RULE `name` against the system database (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Drop auth rule
description: DropAuthRuleIfExists issues CYPHER 25 DROP AUTH RULE `name` IF EXISTS against the system database during Neo4jAuthRule deletion cleanup (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Validate Neo4jUser spec
description: UserValidator.Validate enforces the Neo4j username shape/length, requires at least one auth provider (passwordSecretRef or externalAuth), rejects the reserved 'system' username and the 'native' externalAuth provider, WARNS (without rejecting) when the username is the default bootstrap admin 'neo4j' because managing it rewrites the credential the operator itself authenticates with, and reports a not-yet-applied password Secret as a transient Pending gap rather than a Failed error (internal/validation/user_validator.go).

name: Validate Neo4jRole spec
description: RoleValidator.Validate enforces the Neo4j role-name pattern, requires spec.adoptBuiltin=true to manage a built-in role name, requires every spec.privileges entry to start with GRANT/DENY and end with `TO <this role>`, and rejects property-based-access-control privileges that target a Neo4jShardedDatabase (internal/validation/role_validator.go).

name: Validate Neo4jRoleBinding spec
description: RoleBindingValidator.Validate enforces the shared username shape check, requires spec.roles to be non-empty with no blank entries, and warns (never errors) when PUBLIC is listed since it is implicit and always ignored (internal/validation/rolebinding_validator.go).

name: Validate Neo4jAuthRule spec
description: AuthRuleValidator.Validate enforces the auth-rule name pattern, requires spec.condition to be a pure expression free of DDL keywords (CREATE/DROP/ALTER/GRANT/DENY/REVOKE/SHOW/RENAME/semicolon) to block Cypher injection, and requires at least one entry in spec.grantedRoles (internal/validation/authrule_validator.go).

name: Reconcile AuraInstance
description: Top-level AuraInstanceReconciler.Reconcile loop: resolves credentials, handles the paused annotation and finalizer, dispatches to create/adopt, drift, tier-upgrade, pause/resume and deletion, then writes status.atProvider plus the Ready/Synced conditions.

name: Create or adopt Aura instance
description: observeOrCreate: lists instances by name to adopt before creating (avoiding a duplicate paid instance), validates the type/region/cloudProvider combo against the project's instance_configurations, and creates via v1 CreateInstance or, when spec.multiDatabase is true, via v2beta1 CreateInstanceV2 (createMultiDatabaseInstance in aura_multidatabase.go).

name: Resize/patch Aura instance
description: reconcileDrift: PATCHes memory, storage, name, secondariesCount and cdcEnrichmentMode when they diverge from the observed instance, gated by the Update management policy.

name: Pause Aura instance
description: reconcilePauseResume: calls PauseInstance when spec.paused=true and the observed instance is running.

name: Resume Aura instance
description: reconcilePauseResume: calls ResumeInstance when spec.paused=false and the observed instance is paused.

name: Upgrade Aura instance tier
description: reconcileUpgrade: performs the single supported in-place tier upgrade (professional-db to business-critical) via UpgradeInstance when spec.type requests it; the CRD's CEL transition rule already rejects every other type change.

name: Delete/orphan Aura instance
description: handleDeletion: honours deletionPolicy (Delete calls DeleteInstance unless deletionProtection is set; Orphan, the default, leaves the cloud instance running) before releasing the finalizer.

name: Reconcile AuraSnapshot
description: AuraSnapshotReconciler.Reconcile: requests a snapshot exactly once via CreateSnapshot, then polls GetSnapshot until Completed/Failed/Cancelled; the create response carries only snapshot_id so the initial phase is recorded as Pending rather than copying fields that are not yet present.

name: Reconcile AuraRestore
description: AuraRestoreReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the target AuraInstance and a snapshot (spec.snapshotId or an AuraSnapshot ref), waits for the instance to be Running, calls RestoreSnapshot, then drives Pending->Restoring->Completed/Failed and never re-fires once terminal.

name: Reconcile AuraDatabase
description: AuraDatabaseReconciler.Reconcile: resolves org/project/instance coordinates from the referenced AuraInstance (which must have been created with multiDatabase:true), refuses creation when the instance's probed multiDatabase verdict is explicitly false, and otherwise creates/adopts the database by the external-database-id annotation since the v2beta1 API returns no database names to adopt by.

name: Reconcile AuraDatabaseBackup
description: AuraDatabaseBackupReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the target database via spec.databaseRef, takes the backup exactly once via CreateDatabaseBackup, then polls GetDatabaseBackup, treating only Completed/Failed as terminal and never inferring completion from an empty just-scheduled status.

name: Reconcile AuraDatabaseRestore
description: AuraDatabaseRestoreReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the database and backup (by spec.backupId or an AuraDatabaseBackup ref), persists a Submitting marker before calling RestoreDatabase (the destructive, non-idempotent call), and records Submitted (not Completed, since v2beta1 exposes no way to observe restore completion) or RestoreOutcomeUnknown if the process died mid-flight.

name: Reconcile Aura org/project member
description: AuraOrganizationMemberReconciler.Reconcile and its AuraProjectMemberReconciler counterpart find an existing Aura console user by email (ListOrgMembers/ListProjectMembers), update their org or project role when it drifts from spec.role, and remove membership on CR deletion; a project member with no project membership yet but an existing org membership is added via AddProjectMember rather than requiring a fresh invite.

name: Reconcile AuraInvite
description: AuraInviteReconciler.Reconcile: builds the two-slot invite body (an organization-* role plus an optional namespace-* project role, refusing a project-only invite since Aura requires an organization role on every invite), adopts a matching pending invite by email+project scope, and since v2beta1 has no GET /invites/{id}, observes status via FindInvite over the LIST endpoint, reporting Sent/Accepted/Revoked/Expired/Declined/Gone.

name: Validate Aura credentials
description: AuraProviderConfigReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the referenced credentials Secret, forces a token exchange and a real ListInstances call to prove the credentials work, and reports CredentialsValidated/CredentialsInvalid on the Ready condition every 10 minutes.

name: Call Aura API (shared client)
description: auraClientForCreds / resolveClient family: returns a shared *aura.Client per credential (keyed by baseURL+clientID+sha256(secret)[:8]) with one OAuth token cache and rate-limit budget (default 25/min), instrumented via metrics.RecordAuraAPICall, that every Aura reconciler's ClientFactory wraps to call ListInstances/CreateInstance/PatchInstance/GetSnapshot/etc.

name: Reconcile AuraCustomerManagedKey
description: AuraCustomerManagedKeyReconciler.Reconcile: adopts an existing key by matching keyId/region/cloudProvider/instanceType (the LIST endpoint returns only summaries, so each name-matched candidate is fetched by GetCustomerManagedKey to confirm before adopting), otherwise creates one, then polls to Ready and on deletion either orphans or deregisters (refused with KeyInUse while any instance still uses it).

name: Reconcile AuraIPFilter
description: AuraIPFilterReconciler.Reconcile: resolves spec.instanceRefs to Aura instance IDs, adopts an existing filter by name or creates one via CreateIPFilter, then converges allow_list/filtered_entities/name/filteringDisabled drift via UpdateIPFilter, and on deletion deletes or orphans the filter.

name: Reconcile Neo4jPlugin
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves clusterRef, refuses to install when another CR in the namespace already targets the same clusterRef with the same plugin name (older CR by creationTimestamp wins), then merges the plugin into the target's env/init-containers. On reaching Ready it records status.installedVersion (the spec.version it installed) and status.installationTime (set once per installed version, not touched by later reconciles or same-version Ready/Installing cycles); a plugin already Ready before those fields existed is backfilled on its next reconcile.

name: Merge NEO4J_PLUGINS list
description: MergeNeo4jPluginList live-patches the target StatefulSet's NEO4J_PLUGINS env var to add/remove this plugin without wholesale-replacing the list, so it never clobbers a value another Neo4jPlugin/Aura Fleet controller wrote.

name: Reconcile CCDR Proxy
description: Creates/updates the CCDR proxy's ConfigMap/Deployment/Service (or tears them down when disabled), then publishes status.crossClusterReplication.{ready,addresses,loadBalancerHostname} from the proxy Service's LoadBalancer ingress before the server ConfigMap is rendered.

name: Create Replica Database From Network
description: Calls CreateReplicaDatabaseFromNetwork with the upstream database name and an address list — either source.addresses directly, or resolved by sf-resolve-upstream-cluster-ref from source.upstreamClusterRef — when the target database does not yet exist (source.mode: network).

name: Resolve Upstream Cluster Ref
description: When source.upstreamClusterRef is set, reads the named Neo4jEnterpriseCluster's status.internalAddresses via a live Get and returns it as the network-mode address list; a missing or not-yet-ready upstream is reported Pending and retried rather than failed, since the upstream may simply not have reconciled yet.

name: Resolve Upstream Backup Ref
description: When source.upstreamBackupRef is set, reads the named Neo4jBackup CR's status.replicationPullURI via a live Get and returns it as the backup-mode pullURI; a missing Neo4jBackup or one that hasn't run its first backup yet is reported Pending and retried rather than failed.

name: CLI Validate
description: Runs the operator's own validators (internal/validation) over manifest files before they are applied, offline for the 21 validators that never touch the client and connected for the cross-reference ones. Distinguishes errors, warnings and Pending, prints the ruleset version it carries, and warns on skew against the operator running in the cluster. It also reports every key a kind has no field for, with its full path, by walking the document against the type's json tags, descending into lists of objects and reporting the item index (spec.topology.serverRoles[0].modeContraint) — open maps (spec.config, driverSettings), metadata and status are skipped, since their keys are data rather than field names.

name: CLI Preflight
description: Checks the cluster-side preconditions a manifest depends on and that no manifest-level check can see: the StorageClass exists and allows volume expansion, a Ready node can fit the memory request, imagePullSecrets exist, and a backup's credentials Secret carries every key the Job mounts or its ServiceAccount carries a cloud-identity annotation; a PVC-backed backup's named claim must exist, except that an absent claim is reported as waiting rather than failed when spec.storage.pvc.size is set, because the operator provisions it in that case, and a claim that cannot be read is a warning rather than a pass or a failure. It also checks the cloud substrate: the provider is detected from a node's spec.providerID, and a CCDR proxy asking for a private load balancer is reported as a problem when the detected provider reads none of the internal-LB annotations the operator emits, or when the Service was already assigned a public address; the cluster default StorageClass is resolved and expansion-checked when spec.storage.className is empty; a hard zone constraint is checked against the zones that exist; and a spec.securityContext override is checked against the namespace's pod-security enforce level, since the override replaces the operator's hardened default rather than merging with it. Each manifest is checked in its own metadata.namespace, as kubectl apply would place it; -n (or the kubeconfig namespace) applies only to manifests that omit one. Checks shape, never reachability: it contacts no bucket, registry or endpoint and runs no probe pod.

name: CLI Status
description: Lists every Neo4j resource in a namespace with phase, readiness and age, taking the kind list from the registered scheme so a new CRD appears without code changes. An unrecognised phase is not treated as a problem, and Pending messages are shown as guidance rather than failure. With --problems it lists the phases Failed, Error, Invalid, Degraded and Unknown, decided from the phase alone (status.ready is omitempty and never stores false); the message block under the table covers only the rows shown.

name: CLI Diagnose
description: Explains why a resource is unhealthy at the Kubernetes level: unschedulable pods, OOMKills (kubelet reason or exit code 137) and non-zero exits, read from both the previous and the current container state so a Job pod under RestartPolicyNever (which never restarts, leaving its last state empty) is reported with the plain log command and, for a backup, the Neo4jBackup's own spec.options.resources, image-pull and crash-loop states (a crash-looping container is not reported twice), unbound PVCs, failed backup Jobs (judged by the Job's Failed and Complete conditions rather than the cumulative status.failed attempt count, so a backup that retried and then completed is not an error; the leftover failed pods of a Job that did not fail are softened to warning or waiting findings), warning events, and custom resources the operator has never written status to. Finds workloads through the operator's exported selectors and anchors rules to Kubernetes API constants where they exist. Exits 1 when a problem is found.

name: CLI Explain
description: Decodes a status condition, phase or condition REASON into what it means and what to do, keyed off the operator's exported condition constants so a rename breaks the build rather than leaving the explanation stale. A live resource's conditions are printed with their reason, explained after the condition's general guidance since the reason is the more specific signal; only reasons that are not guessable from the string itself get an entry. Negative-polarity conditions (ClusterNotReady, Degraded, ServersPendingDrain, UserNotFound, PendingDependencies, AuthRuleVersionTooOld) are marked healthy when False, and their problem guidance is shown only when True. Reports unrecognised terms as unrecognised, naming its own version.

name: CLI Connect and Cypher
description: Resolves how to reach a deployment — admin Secret, pod and container, and the Bolt scheme from the deployment kind and spec.tls (neo4j/neo4j+s routing for a cluster, bolt/bolt+s for a standalone) — and either prints the connection details or hands over an interactive cypher-shell session via kubectl exec. The printed details give the same in-cluster address the session dials; for a port-forward under TLS they say that the certificate never names localhost and offer the +ssc variant for local testing only. The password is referenced by env var inside the pod and never passes through this process or the audit log.

name: CLI Export Replica Database
description: Authors a Neo4jReplicaDatabase manifest for a downstream on a DIFFERENT Kubernetes cluster, filling source.pullURI from an upstream Neo4jBackup's status.replicationPullURI or source.addresses from an upstream cluster's cross-cluster replication status. Same-cluster users are pointed back at upstreamBackupRef and upstreamClusterRef, which the operator resolves live. Output is validated with the operator's own ReplicaValidator before it is printed.

name: CLI Support Bundle
description: Collects custom resources, workloads, events and pod logs into one redacted archive. Secret values, last-applied-configuration annotations and sensitive-looking literal environment variables are never included; valueFrom references are kept because they explain failures and hold no secret. Every redaction is enumerated in REDACTIONS.txt. Collection is best-effort: every read that fails (a CR-kind, events, pods, secrets-listing, container-log or operator read) is skipped without aborting and listed, as the read plus its error text only, in errors.txt, and the command prints how many reads failed.

name: Normalise Role Privileges
description: normaliseDesired() maps each spec.privileges statement to the rows Neo4j actually stores for it (lists expanded, plurals singularised, default segments filled, verbs renamed, database names lower-cased, aliases resolved), using a probe of the statement on a throwaway role, cached per target UID, image and alias map with a 1h TTL. Statements naming a missing database, or whose probe fails, fall back to textual canonicalisation (internal/controller/neo4jrole_normalise.go).

name: Probe privilege rendering
description: ProbePrivilegeRendering creates a throwaway operator_privilege_probe_<random> role, grants one privilege statement to it, reads SHOW ROLE PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS back and drops the role, all in one system-database session so the read is causally after the grant (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Learn Role Privileges
description: Learn mode (--privilege-normalisation=learn, the default; the probe is opt-in): reconcileLearned()/learnDesired() learn each spec statement's stored rows from the operator's own grant (before/after diff), persist them in status.privilegeRenderings BEFORE any revoke, never revoke status.unattributedPrivileges, and re-learn on scope change, a vanished unattributed row, or revocation of a removed statement's rows. Fails loudly when the installed CRD prunes these status fields (internal/controller/neo4jrole_learn.go).

name: Grant and read privileges
description: GrantAndReadPrivileges runs SHOW ROLE PRIVILEGES, one GRANT/DENY, and SHOW again in a single system-database session, returning the before/after rows so learn mode can attribute exactly the rows the statement created; transient 25N11 conflicts retry the whole sequence (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Reconcile Server Shortfall
description: Sets the status of a cluster that is not fully formed. Feeds the formation result, the ClusterFormed memory, whether a template rollout is in flight and the Degraded condition's lastTransitionTime to the shortfall assessment, then writes Ready (Degraded condition True) within the grace period, Degraded past it, or Forming — for first formation, rollouts, scale-ups, split-brain or the loss of a majority (#444). ClusterDegraded and ClusterQuorumLost are deduplicated in memory, since the informer cache can return the previous phase.

name: Assess Server Shortfall
description: Pure decision for a formed cluster short of servers: a server that stays Enabled in SHOW SERVERS but is not Available is lost, one never Enabled is joining. With more than half the expected servers available the verdict is WithinGrace, then Degraded once the shortfall outlasts the grace period; half or fewer is QuorumLost; never formed, a rollout, a split-brain, Neo4j unreachable or fewer Enabled servers than expected is Forming.
